The hard EIC query carries no number and none of the answer's wording ('$11,950', 'investment income') beyond the corpus-wide credit name, and its answer sits in p596/02 'Rules for Everyone' while every p596 chapter discusses eligibility.

queries.q: How long do I have to own and live in my house before I can sell it without paying tax on the profit?
queries.expect: If you owned the home and used it as your residence for at least 24 months of the previous 5 years

queries.q: Can I count the miles I drive to medical appointments as a medical deduction, and at what rate?
queries.expect: If you don’t want to use your actual expenses for 2025, you can use the standard medical mileage rate of 21 cents a mile.

queries.q: I just took a second job — what do I need to do about my withholding so I don't end up owing at tax time?
queries.expect: If you have income from more than one job at the same time, or are married filing jointly and you and your spouse both work

queries.q: Is any of the college tuition credit refundable if I don't owe income tax this year?
queries.expect: Forty percent of the American opportunity credit may be refundable

queries.q: I only made about $19,000 working part-time, but I sold some stock this year — can I still get the earned income credit?
queries.expect: You can’t claim the EIC unless your investment income is $11,950 or less.
